text:
alex: quick RFC follow-up — proposal to simplify auth checks for the dashboard query fast-path. TL;DR: push minimal RBAC (route-level allowlist + tenant match) into gateway, move complex entitlements to async verifier + cache. latency wins, tradeoffs on surface area. thoughts?

maria: curious — what specific checks are you proposing we move? can we avoid leaking tenant-scoped data? :thinking:

alex: plan: keep tenant ownership and basic read-scope inline. move attribute-based entitlements (role->column mapping, feature gating, row-level expressions) to async verifier and a short-lived cache. fast-path will return a minimal safe projection for most dashboard widgets; full projection gets backfilled if verifier confirms.

sam: isn't returning a minimal projection risky for consumers? dashboards expect certain fields and break quietly. we've seen this in the past.

alex: good point. mitigation: client-side projection shim. UI receives `partial=true` and shows placeholders for redacted fields + skeleton. it then issues a follow-up fetch for the delta. opt-in per route so legacy dashboards unaffected.

qin: can you share perf numbers you used to make the call?

alex: local traces on read-heavy workload: baseline (full inline checks) p50=12ms p95=40ms p99=75ms. gateway minimal checks + async verify + cache: p50=14ms p95=20ms p99=24ms. stable across tenants in load test. big win at p99.

maria: auditability & compliance: synchronous checks are nice because they're easy to prove later. do we lose evidence if verification is async?

alex: we keep audit events for fast-path decisions synchronously. async verifier emits a cross-check audit event and will generate an alert if it disagrees. each event includes request id, auth-hash and ent-version. snippet: 

```
// fast-path auth pseudocode
if (routeAllow(request.route) && tenantMatch(req.tenant)) {
  emitAudit(req.id, 'fast-allow', user);
  spawnAsync(() => verifyDetailedEntitlements(req));
  return partialProjection();
}
```

sam: what's the behaviour if async verifier later denies a request that was already served partially? do we redact retroactively?

alex: we won't mutate previously delivered UI state. instead: we mark the record as `revoked` and on next fetch the client will replace/redact the sensitive fields and surface a notice. we also invalidate the cache for the user/tenant/ent-version combo. entitlement version is bumped on policy changes.

maria: deployment & cutover plan? need clear rollback triggers.

alex: feature-flag rollout: `fast_auth_path` per-tenant.
Stage 1: internal tenants + engineering dashboards only, monitor audit diffs and partial-replacement rate.
Stage 2: non-sensitive product dashboards opt-in.
Stage 3: global enable with guard rails.
Rollback if mismatch rate > 0.1% or partial-replacement > 1% for > 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy started: featureflag/gateway/fast_auth_path -> canary group alpha (3 hosts) :rocket:

qin: we need a strict interface contract between gateway and query-service. gateway should attach `auth-hash`, `ent-version`, and `partial-ok` headers. query-service must be tolerant to missing headers and default to full-check path.

alex: agreed. RFC addendum will include header schema: 

``
X-Auth-Hash: sha256(<user|roles|time>)
X-Ent-Version: v<number>
X-Partial-Ok: true
```

sam: add metrics: `fast_path.hit`, `fast_path.miss`, `async_verify.pass`, `async_verify.fail`, `partial_replace.count`. need SLO alerting wires.

maria: security ok with Infosec/legal for PII? partial results could surface metadata.

alex: talked to legal — allowed if we redact PII fields and include a link to data access request in the response. responses must carry a `compliance-tag` and `outcome` field. HSM/KMS flows unchanged.

qin: follow-up tasks list?

alex: 1) Add header schema + tolerant parsing in gateway & query-service.
2) Emit sync audit event on fast-allow + async cross-check event.
3) Feature flag scaffolding + canary wiring.
4) UI partial-projection UX + client shim.
5) Metrics + SLO dashboards + alerts.
6) Runbook for mismatch and rollback.
7) Docs & RFC addendum.
I'll open PRs for 1,2 and 3 today.

maria: add SLO acceptance in the PRs (target p99 < 30ms for dashboard queries) :thumbsup:

alex: will do. thanks!

sam: one more nit: ensure the gateway keeps a local LRU cache for ent-hash -> allow decision, TTL short (30s) and proactively warms on tenant heavy traffic. avoids stampeding.

alex: good call. add to tasks.

maria: thanks everyone. please link PRs here once opened.
